findings.issue: C8 requires a test showing the gateway does not route /internal/**. No gateway file is in the PR-B diff, and evidence.md does not mention this. The condition is in fact covered by the existing GatewayEdgeIntegrationTest.internalPathsAreNotRouted: anonymous gets 401, an authenticated caller with a spoofed X-Internal-Token gets 404, and the stub downstream is never hit. The gateway route table is also an explicit allow-list: the discovery locator is pinned false at application.yml:74, and the payment route matches only /api/payments, /api/wallet and /api/gift-cards. The trouble is that the existing test uses /internal/carts/..., not the new /internal/wallet/credits/{key}, and nothing in the PR's evidence points to it.
findings.fix: Record in evidence.md and pr.md that C8's gateway item is met by GatewayEdgeIntegrationTest.internalPathsAreNotRouted. Optionally parameterise that test to also try GET /internal/wallet/credits/return-rest-<uuid>, so the new path is pinned explicitly.

findings.issue: For C6, differentAmount and differentCurrency only assert isInstanceOf(CodedException.class). A 503 (DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE) would also pass them, for example from a lookup stub that stopped matching, or from the ensure or collect path failing. differentUser checks RESOURCE_CONFLICT, but these two do not, so they do not prove that the mismatch rule is what produced the 409.
findings.fix: Use the same isInstanceOfSatisfying(CodedException.class, e -> assertThat(e.errorCode()).isEqualTo(ErrorCode.RESOURCE_CONFLICT)) as differentUser.

findings.issue: C5 says the legacy lookup must never apply to DIRECT_WALLET. That route also credits under return-rest-<id> (ReturnService.callRefund:164), so a wrong gate would turn every wallet-order refund into a 'legacy paid' no-op. The gate is correct ("PAYMENT_WALLET".equals(plan.route())), but no test pins it. codRows is a mock in ReturnServiceRefundTest, and the DIRECT_WALLET case there never verifies it. The COD_PENDING/NONE case is covered (codPendingMovesNothing), but DIRECT_WALLET is not.
findings.fix: In the existing DIRECT_WALLET test (and one PAYMENT_SOURCE case), add verify(codRows, never()).prepareRefund(any()). Optionally add a guard demo with the gate mutated to route != NONE.

findings.issue: exactMatch uses wallet "0", so the legacy-paid path is never exercised together with a wallet leg. The design relies on the wallet leg replaying return-wallet-<id> (the same key as pre-F-09, as confirmed in the F-09 design) and on the legacy-paid rest counting as siblingRest for later returns. Neither the AC-12 test listed in the design (100 total / 30 wallet, pre-V13 REFUNDED 40 + new 60) nor a cap test that includes a legacy-credited sibling is present. capHoldsAcrossReturns proves the general cap only, with rows and no legacy credit.
findings.fix: Add one case: a COD order with a wallet part, return A legacy-paid by an exact return-rest credit, then return B refunded normally. Assert one creditWallet per return-wallet key, no refund for A, and that the rest sent for B is at most total - wallet - A.rest.

findings.issue: prepareRefund decides 'collected' from deliveredAt != null plus paymentStatus, but OrderStore.route sends a COD order to PAYMENT_WALLET on paymentStatus alone. A COD_COLLECTED order with a null delivered_at (data anomaly) would be ensured but never collect-marked, so payment-service answers 409 'COD pending'. That fails loudly with no money moved, so it is safe, but the two rules are inconsistent.
findings.fix: Optional: derive 'collected' from paymentStatus alone in codRowSpec, or log the anomaly at WARN when route is PAYMENT_WALLET but collected is false.

findings.issue: The 409 procedure says 'close the return by hand'. The F-09 pr.md warns that a manual REFUNDED flip skips the stock release and the RETURN_REFUNDED event. This runbook does not repeat that warning.
findings.fix: Add a sentence: a manual close must also release the returned stock and record the event, as in the F-09 note.

findings.issue: Fully-qualified names are used where an import would do: GetMapping here, and com.acme...Outbox and java.util.concurrent.* in CodPaymentRowsIntegrationTest. The PR-A nit that touched this file fixed the @JsonIgnoreProperties FQN but added a new FQN.

The guard demos are real assertion failures (M1: 'Expecting code to raise a throwable' and NeverWantedButInvoked refund; M2: the cap sum; M3: NeverWantedButInvoked ensureRow; M4: 200 not in [401,403]; M5: the config class list). However, the two new behaviour switches in PR-B have no demo: collect's collected-state guard (undeliveredNotCollected), and the relay COD_COLLECTED -> codRows.collect switch (relayCollect would fail on the base call). There is also no CEO forge-verify record for 8ff2913 yet.
findings.fix: Optionally add M6 (drop the collected check) and M7 (relay back to remote.codCollectedNow), and record forge-verify --changed for 8ff2913 before the PR is called done.

summary: I recommend approve: there are no blocker or major findings, and every PR-B AC (AC-6 to AC-12, AC-14) is met. PR-B follows the accepted design and CTO conditions C1 to C8. C5: runLegs calls prepareRefund before the wallet leg and before any refund, on every attempt whose route is PAYMENT_WALLET and whose rest leg is not yet SUCCEEDED. It also runs when the row already exists (differentUser and exactMatch use withRow=true). prepareRefund returns at once for non-COD orders, and DIRECT_WALLET never reaches it. C6: an exact match (same user, amount by compareTo with '100' against 100.00, same currency) sets the rest leg SUCCEEDED with no ensure and no refund, and a retry stays quiet. Any mismatch logs 'COD LEGACY CREDIT MISMATCH' at ERROR with ids only, and answers 409 before money moves; the tests assert never refund and never walletCredit, and the return stays PICKED_UP. A lookup 404 from an old payment-service proceeds when the order has a row, and gives 503 when it has none. AC-12: freezeLegs is unchanged and still caps the rest leg at total - wallet - siblingRest. capHoldsAcrossReturns proves wallet credits sum to 100 and refunds to 200 with retries paying nothing, and the M2 mutant breaks it. A legacy-paid rest is never sent again. C3: collect runs ensure, then calls codCollectedNow only on CREATED or EXISTING and only when the order state is delivered and COD_COLLECTED, PARTIALLY_REFUNDED or REFUNDED. Cancelled orders get SKIPPED_CANCELLED, with no ensureRow call and no mark. Undelivered orders get a row but are never marked. codCollected on payment-service is a conditional update, so repeat marks are no-ops. The relay COD_COLLECTED case now calls codRows.collect. C2, C4 and C7: the runbook has the exact UPDATE ... WHERE id IN (SELECT id ... WHERE kind='COD_COLLECTED' AND status='DEAD' ORDER BY created_at, seq LIMIT 500). I checked every column against V10. It also has the drain check, the rowless-legacy note and the 409 procedure, with queries against real columns (rest_leg_amount from V13). C8: the endpoint returns only found, userId, amount and currency; it logs nothing; it is protected by InternalTokenFilter, with tests for a missing, wrong or empty token and a positive case; it is listed in endpoints.md; and there is no springdoc to leak it. The gateway not-routed test is not in the diff, but the existing GatewayEdgeIntegrationTest.internalPathsAreNotRouted covers /internal/** under the allow-list routing, so this is a minor finding to record, not missing coverage. All earlier minors are resolved. From the PR-A review: the @Version bypass (version + 1 in the JPQL), the order-dependent ensureRow counts (now argThat by order id), the PaymentRow decode test, the duplicated INSERT (now delegates), the FQN annotation, and a WARN for a missing order. The kind-list seam nit was kept, as accepted. From the PR-A security review: NoUserTokenFeignConfig is added to PaymentFeignClient, with a header test and a positive control. The 60 s stray-row note is in the runbook. WARN is changed to ERROR. A COD ensure over a non-COD row now returns at once with no Razorpay wait, and that is tested. Concurrency is fine: ensure holds no transaction or row lock around remote calls, which is proven by the blocked-latch test. Two concurrent ensures give one CREATED and one EXISTING. The refund lease serialises refund attempts. The findings are minor test-strength gaps: the 409 code is not asserted in two mismatch tests; nothing pins that DIRECT_WALLET skips the lookup; and there is no legacy-paid case with a wallet part and a sibling.
